description: This bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance, measured as MAP@10, for two sampling strategies – “Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy” and “Uniform Sampling Strategy” – across five values of ‘m’, ranging from 6 to 10. The horizontal axis is labeled “m” and displays the categories 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 in ascending order without a defined scale type. The vertical axis is labeled “MAP@10”, has a linear scale ranging from 23.0 to 27.0 with tick labels spaced at 0.5 intervals, and no stated units.  For each value of ‘m’, there are two bars representing the two sampling strategies: purple for “Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy” and yellow for “Uniform Sampling Strategy”. The purple bars, representing the “Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy”, have heights of approximately 25.8, 26.2, 26.1, 26.4, and 26.5 for m values of 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10, respectively. The yellow bars, representing the “Uniform Sampling Strategy”, have heights of approximately 24.3, 24.6, 25.2, 24.8, and 24.5 for m values of 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10, respectively. The bars are arranged in pairs, one purple and one yellow, grouped by the value of m. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
